O · GloSIS

The federation now has working parts

A shared language

The ISO 28258 data model, the GloSIS web ontology and its open code lists.

Unchanged, and now built into the software.

A node in a box

OpenNSIS: an open-source national soil information system that speaks those standards from the first day.

Installed by the country, on the country's server.

A place to look

The Discovery Hub: one map showing what each node publishes, fetched from the node when someone asks.

In development, already answering.

The principle has not moved: data stay in the country, under the country's rules. What is new is that it runs.

A · OpenNSIS

Where it runs today

7

National servers

Bangladesh · Indonesia · Kyrgyzstan · Lao PDR · Philippines · Sri Lanka · Thailand

Operated by national institutions, on their own infrastructure.

7

Demonstration instances

Ghana · Guatemala · Honduras · Kenya · Mozambique · Tunisia · Zambia

For the SoilFER project, until a national server takes over.

10

Training instances

One per group, created for a single day of practice.

Maputo, 19 November 2026.

Bhutan, Cambodia, Nepal, Uzbekistan and Viet Nam run national systems of their own. Directory of instances: http://5.223.62.255/

A · OpenNSIS

New since September

Public website

Every instance serves its own site, with home, news, catalogue, statistics, people and contact pages edited from the admin panel.

Catalogue page

Each map as a card with its licence, its download and its WMS address: the same records that harvesters read.

Laboratory link

Results arrive from the laboratory system (LIMS) with uncertainty and detection limits; values below detection stay marked as such.

Sampling design

SoilFER three-stage designs drawn on the map, generated, and published as layers with point export.

Easier uploads

A spreadsheet template with the rules written in, and a review that shows only the profiles with errors.

Faster maps

Raster maps served as cached tiles, in a redesigned interface with light and dark themes.

The full record, feature by feature: github.com/un-fao/OpenNSIS/blob/main/NEWS.md

B · Discovery Hub

How the Hub connects the nodes

Anyone looking for soil dataplanners · researchers · partners
↓
GloSIS Discovery Hubharvests metadata · checks that nodes are alive · searches by area
↓  standard requests, over the Internet
CatalogueOGC API – Records · CSW
MapsWMS
GloSIS APIprofiles and observations · with a token
↑  three doors of the national system, and the data do not leave it
Joining is one Connect button in the OpenNSIS admin panel; the Hub administrator approves. Disconnect pauses sharing at any time.

B · Discovery Hub

What travels, and what stays

WhatHow the Hub gets itKept in the Hub?
Metadata records of the mapsthe node's public catalogue (OGC API – Records)yes, a copy of the record
Summary of soil properties/glosis/manifest (with a token)yes, one line per property
Profile points and observations/glosis/profile · /glosis/observationno, fetched live and cached for 10 minutes
Map images and legendsthe node's WMSno, only relayed

Not only OpenNSIS

Any standard CSW catalogue can be listed, such as GeoNetwork or pyCSW. Standards only, nothing written for one provider.

In the Hub today

Four OpenNSIS demonstration nodes and one external catalogue, ISRIC's, read through plain CSW.

A node that stops answering leaves the results until it is back; nothing is served from an old copy.

R · Next

What comes next

More national nodes

Demonstration instances moving to servers in the country, operated by the national institution.

Numbered releases

National servers updating to tested, tagged versions instead of following the development line.

Laboratory link in routine use

The LIMS connector feeding laboratory results straight into the national system.

A permanent Discovery Hub

Out of development, at a GloSIS address, listing OpenNSIS nodes and standard catalogues alike.

Requests and issues: github.com/un-fao/OpenNSIS/issues

R · Next

How a country joins

1 · Install

One command on a Linux server in the country. It takes 10 minutes to install.

2 · Publish

Load profiles and maps; decide, project by project and map by map, what is public and under which licence.

3 · Connect

One click registers the node with the Hub; one more disconnects it. Nothing is copied away.

Already running a system of your own? A standard CSW catalogue is enough to be listed.
